cds.text: Sort, name and create familiar shapes; recognise familiar shapes in the environment and give reasons
Make, compare and classify familiar shapes; recognise shapes and objects in the environment and identify similarities and differences
Recognise, compare and classify shapes by number of sides, using terms such as opposite, parallel, curved and straight
Describe the position of oneself and objects relative to other people and objects in a familiar space
Give and follow directions to move people and objects to different locations within a space
Locate positions on two-dimensional representations of a familiar space; move positions by following directions and pathways

sentences.text: {{S}} follows simple directions to move to a new position.
{{S}} uses words such as 'under', 'next to' and 'behind' to describe where objects are.
{{S}} gives and follows directions between familiar places, using turns to the left or right.
{{S}} reads simple maps and plans a path from one place to another.
{{S}} describes a path on a map using important places and compass directions.
{{S}} responds to simple instructions about position or movement.
{{S}} matches items of similar length and identifies if two lengths are the same or different.
{{S}} identifies and names common two-dimensional shapes.
{{S}} names basic shapes in {{pos}} environment and describes their features.
{{S}} makes pictures and designs by fitting shapes together.
{{S}} compares the surfaces of two shapes to see which is bigger.
{{S}} makes shapes by tracing around objects, drawing and building.
{{S}} sorts two-dimensional shapes based on their sides and corners.
{{S}} compares the area of two-dimensional shapes by using counters and blocks.
{{S}} slides, flips and turns shapes, recognising that the shape stays the same size.
{{S}} creates rows and columns to model the area of rectangles.
{{S}} compares and describes the features of shapes, such as parallel sides or equal sides.
{{S}} finds lines of symmetry in pictures, designs and shapes.
{{S}} creates grid structures to model the area of rectangles.
{{S}} creates patterns by flipping, sliding and turning shapes.
{{S}} compares the areas of shapes by estimating first, then measuring on a square grid.
{{S}} combines shapes to make new shapes and designs.
{{S}} splits a shape into smaller shapes and describes the result.
{{S}} points to a square, triangle, circle or rectangle when asked and matches them to images.
{{S}} sorts shapes into groups.
{{S}} identifies basic three-dimensional objects and describes their features.
{{S}} describes and compares three-dimensional objects.
{{S}} names three-dimensional objects including cubes, cylinders, spheres and rectangular prisms.
{{S}} names and describes the features of common three-dimensional objects.
{{S}} participates in whole class activities to sort objects by one feature.
{{S}} experiments with filling and pouring to compare how much containers can hold.
{{S}} predicts which objects will stack and packs blocks into a given space.
{{S}} compares how much space different block models take up.
{{S}} builds shapes from connecting cubes to compare how much space they take up.
{{S}} compares how much different containers can hold using concrete materials.
{{S}} describes the features of prisms, pyramids and cylinders by building models of them.
{{S}} measures how much containers hold in litres, linking the litre to everyday containers.
{{S}} sketches objects from different views and builds models from drawings.
{{S}} orders the amounts different containers can hold that have been measured in millilitres.
{{S}} selects objects by pointing or touching as they are named.
{{S}} matches objects to given shapes.
{{S}} stacks objects such as blocks.
